column5: Look: Cargo Is the Colour. A chunky, rounded, flat-shaded asteroid in chalky pastels under bright sunlight; ore is the only faceted, glossy, fully saturated thing, and richer ore is more saturated. Hot magenta means danger and nothing else: the creatures, and your oxygen gauge when low. Signature detail: your pack glows brighter as it fills. Every figure drawn, no emoji, no plain circles.
References: Astroneer (a colourful, friendly space mood; not its look), Escape from Tarkov (the haul and the loss).
View: 3D · Camera: first person.
First-person mining: rock cracks in stages, ore flies to the pack
One hand-made asteroid: a safe landing area, three zones of rising richness and danger *(provisional)*
Oxygen that drains all run and faster when sprinting
Creatures in the rock that wake from mining noise, 2 kinds *(guessed)*
A limited pack with its worth on screen
The ship as the exit; death loses pack and tool

You step out of your ship onto a sunlit pastel asteroid, drill in hand, oxygen full.
A glossy blue seam glints a few steps away.
You hold the drill on it, the rock cracks in stages, ore pops out and flies into your pack, and the pack's worth ticks up for the first time.
A second seam glints further in, past the edge of the safe landing area, where the rock is darker and something magenta stirs.
The landing area is safe.
Beyond it the threat is constant: oxygen drains the whole run, and creatures sleep in the rock and wake from mining noise near them, so the richest seams, deepest in, are the most dangerous to work.
Running out of oxygen or being killed loses the pack and the tool; you start the next run with a basic drill.
Later, a better drill opens harder rock deeper in.
